data.narrative:
Antares is a Series C nuclear energy company founded by Jordan Bramble and Julia DeWahl that has raised $470M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comp universe of 11 total entities: 3 public peers (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 8 private companies including Oklo, X-Energy, Nano Nuclear Energy, Fuse Energy, and Last Energy operating within the nuclear energy sector.

Stage-progression methodology is the applicable approach here, using the $470M total raised as a proxy baseline and applying a 1.7x multiplier typical for Series C to next-stage advancement in this sector. This method yields an implied valuation of $799M. Peer-median triangulation was not feasible; while four same-sector nuclear peers exist in the dataset, none satisfy the filtering criteria of same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-tier valuation required to generate a statistically meaningful median. Applying an all-sector median would introduce unacceptable sectoral bias.

The triangulation analysis supports a valuation range of $679M (low) to $919M (high), with a median point of $799M. This range reflects the single applicable method and carries inherent uncertainty around the 1.7x step-up multiplier's appropriateness to Antares' specific risk profile and market conditions. Refinement would require either expanded near-peer data at comparable stages or additional corroborating methods (revenue multiples, DCF calibration). Key uncertainties include technology maturity, regulatory pathway clarity, and capital efficiency relative to the broader nuclear cohort.
